external_entities.name: colleague
external_entities.description: A colleague who signs in through the identity broker and uses applications.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.
external_entities.notes: The text does not state whether colleagues are asked for a second factor.

external_entities.name: franchise colleague
external_entities.description: A franchise colleague whose own identity provider vouches for them.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them
external_entities.notes: The text does not state which colleagues the franchise identity provider is allowed to vouch for.

external_entities.name: HR system
external_entities.description: The system from which group membership and leaver changes are pulled overnight.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Group membership is not maintained there by hand — it comes from the HR system overnight.

external_entities.name: identity provider
external_entities.description: The franchise colleagues' own identity provider that vouches for them.
external_entities.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them
external_entities.notes: The text does not state which colleagues this provider is allowed to vouch for.

processes.name: identity broker
processes.description: Signs colleagues in, issues tokens, pulls directory changes, and writes sign-ins to an audit log.
processes.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.
processes.notes: The broker signs tokens with a signing key and accepts the franchise identity provider as a sign-in. The text does not state whether colleagues are asked for a second factor.

processes.name: store admin console
processes.description: An application that uses the token's groups to authorize changing prices and voiding transactions across every store.
processes.source_excerpt: The store admin console is one of those applications.
processes.notes: The console does not check which store the colleague belongs to, so a store-manager token works against every store.

data_stores.name: key store
data_stores.description: The store holding the signing key used by the identity broker.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_stores.name: directory
data_stores.description: The identity broker's directory containing colleagues and their group memberships.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down whether the directory is encrypted where it sits.

data_stores.name: audit log
data_stores.description: The log to which the identity broker writes sign-ins.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down what the log records, whether it covers the franchise route, or whether the log is encrypted where it sits.

data_flows.name: sign-in
data_flows.description: A colleague signs in through the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.

data_flows.name: sign-in
data_flows.description: A franchise colleague signs in through the identity broker using their own identity provider's vouching.
data_flows.source_excerpt: We also let the franchise stores in.
data_flows.notes: Franchise colleagues' own identity provider vouches for them, and the text does not state which colleagues it is allowed to vouch for.

data_flows.name: vouch sign-in
data_flows.description: The franchise identity provider vouches for a franchise colleague's sign-in.
data_flows.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in.
data_flows.notes: The text does not state which colleagues the provider is allowed to vouch for.

data_flows.name: issue token
data_flows.description: The identity broker issues a token to a colleague.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Once the broker has signed a colleague in it issues them a token.
data_flows.notes: The token carries the colleague's staff id and groups. Tokens are good for twelve hours and there is no way to pull one back before it expires.
data_flows.data_description: token containing staff id and group list

data_flows.name: issue token
data_flows.description: The identity broker issues a token to a franchise colleague.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the broker takes that as a sign-in.
data_flows.notes: The text does not explicitly state the token issuance step for franchise colleagues, but says the broker takes the identity provider's vouching as a sign-in.
data_flows.data_description: token containing staff id and group list

data_flows.name: change prices and void transactions
data_flows.description: A colleague uses a store-manager token at the store admin console to change prices and void transactions.
data_flows.source_excerpt: If the token has the store-manager group in it, the console lets the holder change prices and void transactions.
data_flows.notes: The console does not check which store the colleague belongs to, so a store-manager token works against every store.

data_flows.name: change prices and void transactions
data_flows.description: A franchise colleague uses a store-manager token at the store admin console to change prices and void transactions.
data_flows.source_excerpt: If the token has the store-manager group in it, the console lets the holder change prices and void transactions.
data_flows.notes: The text does not explicitly say franchise colleagues use the store admin console.

data_flows.name: fetch public key
data_flows.description: The store admin console fetches the public half of the signing key from the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Applications fetch the public half from the broker to check the signature.

data_flows.name: pull changes
data_flows.description: The identity broker pulls group membership and leaver changes from the HR system overnight.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker pulls the changes once a night

data_flows.name: write directory
data_flows.description: The identity broker writes colleagues and group memberships to its directory.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.

data_flows.name: write sign-ins
data_flows.description: The identity broker writes sign-ins to the audit log.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_flows.notes: The text does not state what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network where the identity broker and store admin console run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The broker runs on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: home
trust_boundaries.description: The home location of colleagues' own devices.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: including their own devices at home.

trust_boundaries.name: franchise stores
trust_boundaries.description: The franchise store environment from which franchise colleagues are admitted.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: We also let the franchise stores in.

assumptions.assumption: The directory's contents are confidential because it contains colleagues and their group memberships, which identify or describe people.
assumptions.basis: The source says the directory contains colleagues and the groups they are in.

assumptions.assumption: The key store's contents are confidential because it holds a signing key.
assumptions.basis: The source says the broker keeps a signing key in the key store.

assumptions.assumption: The audit log's contents are confidential because it records sign-ins associated with colleagues.
assumptions.basis: The source says the broker writes sign-ins to the audit log.
